correctness.rationale: For cells of length 1/56, Rπ permutes 7 blocks of 8 cells preserving the internal offset. The first three branches of a are rigid translations aligned with cell boundaries, and its tail on [7/8,1) is exactly the scaled a mapping onto [0,1/8). The three rigid branch ranges avoid that section, so the first tail edge ends each first-return path. I independently computed paths and cycles by applying each branch to exact rational cell boundaries, matching all listed rows and the periodic cycles. For k=0,1,4, complete tower coverage persists along the stated recurring words. Iterating the complete first returns shows every point visits every depth section, with least first return at depth r at least 2ʳ; a finite periodic orbit would meet every section and therefore contain zero, contradicting these growing minimum return times. For k=5,6 the rigid cycles return whole half-open cells by an exact translation with net displacement zero. For k=2,3 the same argument holds in the induced map after one full covering step, so gives nonempty periodic intervals for the original map. Half-open branches justify the endpoint claim, not just almost-everywhere recurrence. Bruin–Lukina Theorem 1.4 gives precisely the stated Lebesgue ergodicity equivalence for this composition and domain.
residual_risks: Incomplete rows do not define a full covering induction for that state; only the exact cycles are needed there. The proof does not determine the full periodic sets or ergodic decompositions.

value.rationale: Cyclic translations form a natural subgroup slice of the permuted-interval family. Its full exact seven-case dichotomy gives both recurrent covering examples and explicitly certified nonergodic examples, and exhibits two distinct initial shifts entering the same recurrent induction and others entering a noncovering state. Exact endpoint-inclusive completeness is useful as a test of induction for non-dyadic rational rotations. Neither the already known k=6 case nor the generic criterion alone supplies that benchmark.
residual_risks: This is a complete cyclic slice at one denominator, not a classification of all 7! permutations or a new general induction theorem.
